title: Isolating identifier equality in a benign native update witness
rationale: A successful same-value update archives its current record in the prior source-informed study. A surgical branch-condition intervention distinguishes that mechanism from a general retrieval or reopen failure.
scope: One implementation, three derived source arms, eight known development streams, one fresh store per cell, sequential calls on one workstation.
research_question: Does gating the dedup repair branch on unequal identifiers prevent the observed current-value disappearance while retaining the distinct-ID behavior?
hypothesis: Same-ID execution of the dedup repair branch is necessary for the observed self-archive witness in the selected streams.
null_hypothesis: Disappearance persists when same-ID execution of this branch is removed, or matched controls change in a way that invalidates the mechanism interpretation.
primary_metric: Successful final call followed by requested-value absence from public, physical, and cold current observations, separately by stream and source arm.
acceptable_evidence: Hash-bound native sources and exact patches, original frozen stream instrument, native return values, stores, separate public and physical observations, cold reopen and worker logs.
intervention: Change only the unique deduplicated update branch condition. Keep native dependencies, literal streams, observations and returned response construction unchanged.
secondary_metrics: Final response with identical id and supersedes
Initial subject remains active when final returned ID differs
gold_reference: Literal values and separate native physical observations. No semantic labels, human annotation or new model calls.
population: Eight previously selected development streams in one pinned implementation. Not independently selected systems or production calls.
sample_size_plan: Three source arms times eight streams times one fresh run: 24 intervention cells. These do not augment the 32-cell unmodified study.
split_policy: The original outcomes are known. This is mechanism testing, not an untouched replication or held-out evaluation.

interventions.distinct_id_guard: Replace the unique if result.get("deduplicated"): branch condition with if result.get("deduplicated") and result["id"] != old_id:.
interventions.dedup_branch_disabled: Replace the same branch condition with if False and result.get("deduplicated"):; this is an experimental negative control, not a repair.

matched_control: All original eight streams retained, including distinct-ID dedup, new-value, archived-value return, namespace and remember controls.
analysis_plan: Report all 24 cells without aggregation into independent bug counts. The returned supersedes field and physical predecessor edges remain separate. Retain null results and any source or observation failures.
failure_criteria: No causal interpretation after source/instrument mismatch, network attempts, native exceptions, sentinel loss, cold drift or failure of the unmodified normal control. Preserve partial captures.
stopping_rule: One fixed 24-cell matrix. No retries, extra repetitions, new systems or paid/model calls in this protocol.
budget: Local cached dependencies and one workstation; zero new model, embedding or paid API calls.
closest_prior_work: Pinned upstream distinct-ID dedup repair and regression tests
Established identifier equality and version-graph principles
OwnMem's retrieval-ablation validation is a different endpoint, not an executed storage baseline
baselines: Whole dedup repair branch disabled as a mechanism control
quality_checks: Instrument and protocol frozen before native calls
Response and stored predecessor kept separate
ethics: Synthetic strings and private stores. No historical source/output rewrite, public disclosure, commit or submission.
interpretation: An isolated source intervention can support a bounded causal mechanism. It cannot establish novel algorithms, complete response-contract repair, production fitness, deployment prevalence or publication readiness.
